dedupe_keys.name: understanding the utility of the ipad pro lidar sensor

description: Understanding the Utility of the iPad Pro LiDAR Sensor is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Joseph Wartman, University of Washington (washington.edu). The project is about assessing the effectiveness of the iPad Pro LiDAR scanner by comparing it to the RTC 360 device. The data can be reused by using the same data while contrasting between data collection methods. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-ev7s-8591. Keywords: LiDAR, iPad Pro, damage, scanner. Published 2021-09-06. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
